TDigest: Quantile sketch optimized for extreme quantiles (p99, p99.9). Most accurate at distribution tails. Only supports FLOAT and DOUBLE inputs. Use when tail latencies or outliers matter — e.g., service-level performance reporting.
Quantiles: Classic mergeable quantile sketch from the original DataSketches paper. Supports all numeric integer/float types. Solid general-purpose choice; KLL is now preferred for new projects.
KLL: Modern quantile sketch — best balance of accuracy, speed, and size. Default choice for general-purpose quantile estimation when you don't have a specific reason to pick TDigest or REQ.
REQ: Quantile sketch with relative-error guarantees. Error scales with rank rather than being fixed, which makes it well-suited for highly skewed data where you want predictable accuracy across the full distribution.
HLL: HyperLogLog distinct-counting sketch. The industry standard — fast serialization/deserialization and broad cross-system compatibility. Choose this when speed and interop matter more than storage.
CPC: Compressed Probability Counting — distinct-counting sketch ~40% smaller than HLL at the same accuracy. Slower to serialize. Choose this when you store many sketches at rest.
Theta: Distinct-counting sketch that supports set operations: union, intersection, and A-not-B (set difference). Use when you need to combine multiple distinct-counts with operations beyond merge.
Frequent Items: Heavy-hitter sketch that identifies the most frequently occurring items in a stream. Returns items along with estimated frequencies and confidence bounds. Use for top-N analysis on high-cardinality streams.
